text:
Maria G: Heads up — staging started spiking after the merge of runtime-autotune (PR #4127). p95 for small-batch short-seq endpoint ~2x. Canary rolled back automatically but alerts still firing.
perf-bot: [ALERT] staging/short-seq p95 latency 220ms -> 480ms over last 5m. Error budget approaching threshold.
Kevin L: I'll bisect now. initial suspicion is autotune heuristic that landed in the PR.
Sanjay K: Seen this pattern before — compile churn + KV cache eviction. If autotune picks a much larger kernel variant we suddenly hit memory pressure and the KV cache starts evicting aggressively.
Olivia R: Reproduced locally on dev-staging with the canary image. Getting repeated kernel compiles:
```
[2026-06-02T14:12:03Z] Compiling kernel: matmul_opt_v8_1.2
[2026-06-02T14:12:03Z] Compiling kernel: matmul_opt_v8_1.2
[2026-06-02T14:12:04Z] Compiling kernel: matmul_opt_v8_1.2
[2026-06-02T14:12:05Z] KV cache miss for prefix hash f3a9... evicting 8 entries
[2026-06-02T14:12:05Z] Compiling kernel: matmul_opt_v9_big
[2026-06-02T14:12:06Z] Compiled kernel matmul_opt_v9_big (35ms)
[2026-06-02T14:12:06Z] Allocated workspace 1.8GB
[2026-06-02T14:12:06Z] KV cache eviction triggered, current size 180MB -> 24MB
```
Kevin L: That log looks like a compile flood: the runtime keeps picking variants that force new JITs and big workspace allocations. The memory pressure then evicts KV cache entries, leading to more recompiles (no prefix cache to use) — positive feedback loop.
Maria G: Any bisect pointer to the exact commit?
Kevin L: Bisect narrowed it to runtime/heuristics commit 9c7b2e9 — autotune scoring change. Repro steps in the bisect: pinned model + short-seq workload + small batch size (1-2).
Sanjay K: I profiled selection scores. Before patch variant scoring normalized factor = 0.8, after patch it's 1.25 for memory-heavy kernels. Result: CPU/mem weight skewed to prefer bigger kernels for short sequences. Profiler snippet:
```
variant matmul_opt_v9_big: score=7.9 (latency_est=3.2, mem_penalty=1.0, norm=1.25)
variant matmul_opt_v8_1.2: score=5.1 (latency_est=4.5, mem_penalty=0.4, norm=0.8)
chosen=matmul_opt_v9_big
```
Olivia R: Also seeing KV cache TTL reset bug in the same deployment: eviction counters spike when the runtime allocates >1GB workspace. That wasn't as visible earlier because we didn't pick the big variant.
Maria G: We need a quick mitigation for canary and staging. Options: revert 9c7b2e9, patch heuristic to restore normalization, or force pin kernel variant list for short-seq route. Thoughts?
Kevin L: Fastest is to pin the heuristic config on staging to previous defaults (deploy config rollback). Command to pin config: `rdwctl config set runtime.autotune.normalization_factor=0.8 --env=staging` — I can run that and roll canary.
deploy-bot: Canary pause issued for deployment abc-2026-06-02-17:40 due to perf alert.
Sanjay K: I recommend revert in mainline as well because this causes cross-route instability. I'll open a revert PR and a follow-up to rework scoring with proper workload-aware normalization.
Kevin L: Rolling config rollback now. Will monitor.
Olivia R: After the rollback pinned normalization_factor=0.8, local repro no longer hits compile flood. p95 back to baseline in staging within 3m.
Maria G: Great. Please file a postmortem with root cause: autotune normalization change + insufficient guard on memory-aware picks + KV cache sensitivity. Assign to runtime/heuristics and eng-sre.
Sanjay K: Filed RETRO-207 with tags: regression, bisect, compile-flood, kvcache. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RETRO-207
Kevin L: PR-REVERT opened: runtime: revert 9c7b2e9.
Maria G: Thanks all. Once revert lands let's run a controlled canary with extended perf checks. :thumbsup:
perf-bot: [RESOLVED] staging/short-seq alert cleared (p95 returned to baseline).
Olivia R: Follow-up: add a unit test that simulates small-batch short-seq workload and asserts kernel selection stays within expected memory envelope.
Kevin L: Agreed — will add test and a CI perf check to catch score shifts.
